domain_characteristics.detection_complexity: high due to rarity and severe class imbalance of R2L and U2R attacks, with difficulty levels ranging from 0 to 18+ indicating variable but often challenging detection
data_characteristics: multi-service (ftp_data, http, telnet, imap4, domain_u, etc.)

common_indicators: elevated 'hot' indicators (e.g., hot >= 1) signaling suspicious system activity
presence of root_shell=1 and num_root > 0 indicating privilege escalation attempts
high rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate values (close to 1.0) associated with rejected connections during attacks like guess_passwd
low or zero src_bytes combined with very high dst_bytes in some R2L attacks (e.g., warezmaster)
flags such as SF (normal finish), RSTO (reset on timeout), and S3 (SYN sent and received) appearing in attack traffic
num_failed_logins > 0 in R2L attack samples indicating brute force or guessing attempts
attack_signatures: Signature 1: R2L attacks often show low src_bytes (0-51), high dst_bytes (thousands to millions), and logged_in=0 or 1 with failed login attempts, e.g., guess_passwd with flag=RSTO and rerror_rate=1.0
Signature 2: U2R attacks characterized by root_shell=1, num_compromised > 0, hot >= 1, and sometimes num_root > 0, often with short or zero duration and services like ftp_data or telnet
Signature 3: High serror_rate and srv_serror_rate near zero in most attacks except guess_passwd where serror_rate can be 0.5, indicating SYN error patterns linked to scanning or brute forcing
technical_markers: src_bytes = 0 combined with dst_bytes > 5000 in warezmaster and similar R2L attacks
rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate >= 0.9 in guess_passwd attacks indicating many rejected connections
hot indicators >= 1 in U2R attacks (loadmodule, buffer_overflow, rootkit)
count and srv_count often low (1-4) in U2R attacks, higher in benign traffic
difficulty_level ranges from 0 to 18, with higher values indicating more subtle or complex attacks
attack_vectors: Exploitation of vulnerable services (ftp_data, telnet, http)
exploit_techniques: Unauthorized file access and command execution

typical_behaviors: Normal connections have src_bytes and dst_bytes > 0 with balanced data flow
Flags predominantly SF indicating normal session establishment and termination
Hot indicators = 0, no suspicious system activity
Logged_in=0 or 1 depending on service, but no privilege escalation markers
Count and srv_count values higher (e.g., count > 10, srv_count > 10) reflecting normal traffic volume
baseline_metrics: src_bytes typically > 20 and dst_bytes > 50 for normal traffic
serror_rate, srv_serror_rate, rerror_rate, srv_rerror_rate all near 0.0
same_srv_rate close to 1.0 indicating consistent service usage
dst_host_count and dst_host_srv_count often high (e.g., 45-255) reflecting normal host activity
difficulty_level high (18-21) for normal samples indicating benign complexity
operational_patterns: Consistent use of common protocols (tcp, udp, icmp) and services (http, domain_u, ftp_data)
Stable connection flags (mostly SF) with low error rates
No unusual spikes in failed logins or hot indicators
Balanced bidirectional traffic (src_bytes and dst_bytes both non-zero and within expected ranges)
Multiple connections to same host and service with high same_srv_rate
normal_thresholds: hot <= 0 to distinguish from suspicious activity
serror_rate < 0.1 and rerror_rate < 0.1 to indicate low error rates
src_bytes > 20 and dst_bytes > 50 to avoid zero or near-zero data flows typical in attacks
count and srv_count > 10 to indicate normal traffic volume

current_threats: Rare and stealthy R2L attacks exploiting remote access vulnerabilities
U2R attacks targeting privilege escalation on compromised hosts
Password guessing and brute force attempts on telnet and ftp services
Rootkit and loadable module based persistence mechanisms
Exploitation of common network services (ftp_data, telnet, http)
emerging_patterns: Increased difficulty levels in detecting U2R attacks indicating evolving stealth techniques
Use of low duration or zero duration connections to evade detection
High error rates (rerror_rate near 1.0) in brute force attacks signaling repeated failed attempts
Sparse but high volume dst_bytes with zero src_bytes in R2L attacks
Consistent use of specific flags (RSTO, SF) in attack traffic
risk_factors: Severe class imbalance complicating detection model training
Low frequency but high impact attacks (rare events)
Use of legitimate services and protocols to mask attacks
Privilege escalation leading to full system compromise
Multiple failed login attempts indicating brute force risks
threat_landscape.threat_sophistication: Moderate to high sophistication with stealthy, low-volume, and privilege escalation attacks requiring advanced detection techniques

detection_rules: Flag connections with hot >= 1 combined with root_shell=1 or num_root > 0 as potential U2R attacks
Alert on rerror_rate or srv_rerror_rate >= 0.9 with flag=RSTO and num_failed_logins > 0 for guess_passwd detection
Detect sessions with src_bytes=0 and dst_bytes > 5000 on ftp_data service as suspicious R2L activity
Monitor for failed login attempts > 0 in combination with logged_in=0 and suspicious flags
Use difficulty_level metadata to prioritize alerts for harder to detect attacks
monitoring_recommendations: Continuously track error rates (serror_rate, rerror_rate) per host and service
Profile normal traffic baselines for count and srv_count to detect anomalies
Monitor privilege escalation indicators (root_shell, num_root, su_attempted)
Correlate hot indicators with login success and failed attempts
Focus on low duration connections with abnormal byte distributions
threshold_suggestions: hot >= 1 for flagging suspicious system activity
rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate >= 0.9 for brute force detection
src_bytes = 0 and dst_bytes > 5000 for R2L detection
num_failed_logins >= 1 combined with logged_in=0 for login attack alerts
serror_rate > 0.1 as potential SYN scan or connection error indicator
pattern_matching: Match sequences of failed login attempts with high rerror_rate and RSTO flags
Identify privilege escalation by matching root_shell=1 with hot > 0 and num_compromised > 0
Detect R2L attacks by matching low src_bytes and high dst_bytes on ftp_data or telnet services
Use temporal connection counts (count, srv_count) to detect bursts or anomalies
Leverage service and protocol combinations with known attack signatures for targeted detection
